Caroline (D5:1): Since we last spoke, some big things have happened. Last week I went to an LGBTQ+ pride parade. Everyone was so happy and it made me feel like I belonged. It showed me how much our community has grown, it was amazing!
Melanie (D5:2): Wow, Caroline, sounds like the parade was an awesome experience! It's great to see the love and support for the LGBTQ+ community. Congrats! Has this experience influenced your goals at all?
Caroline (D5:3): Thanks, Mel! It really motivated me for sure. Talking to the community made me want to use my story to help others too - I'm still thinking that counseling and mental health is the way to go. I'm super excited to give back.
Melanie (D5:4): Wow, Caroline! That's great! I just signed up for a pottery class yesterday. It's like therapy for me, letting me express myself and get creative. Have you found any activities that make you feel the same way? [image: a photo of a person holding a frisbee in their hand]
Caroline (D5:5): Wow, Melanie! I'm getting creative too, just learning the piano. What made you try pottery?
Melanie (D5:6): I'm a big fan of pottery - the creativity and skill is awesome. Plus, making it is so calming. Look at this! [image: a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design]
Caroline (D5:7): That bowl is gorgeous! The black and white design looks so fancy. Did you make it?
Melanie (D5:8): Thanks, Caroline! Yeah, I made this bowl in my class. It took some work, but I'm pretty proud of it.
Caroline (D5:9): Nice job! You really put in the work and it definitely shows. Your creativity looks great!
Melanie (D5:10): Thanks, Caroline! Your kind words mean a lot. Pottery is a huge part of my life, not just a hobby - it helps me express my emotions. Clay is incredible, it brings me so much joy!
Caroline (D5:11): Wow, Mel, I'm so stoked for you that art is helping you express yourself and bring you joy! Keep it up!
Melanie (D5:12): Thanks, Caroline! I'm excited to see where pottery takes me. Anything coming up you're looking forward to?
Caroline (D5:13): Thanks Mel! I'm going to a transgender conference this month. I'm so excited to meet other people in the community and learn more about advocacy. It's gonna be great!
Melanie (D5:14): Sounds awesome, Caroline! Have a great time and learn a lot. Have fun!
Caroline (D5:15): Cool, thanks Mel! Can't wait. I'll keep ya posted. Bye!
Melanie (D5:16): Bye, Caroline! Can't wait to hear about it. Have fun and stay safe!

Caroline (D19:1): Woohoo Melanie! I passed the adoption agency interviews last Friday! I'm so excited and thankful. This is a big move towards my goal of having a family.
Melanie (D19:2): Congrats, Caroline! Adoption sounds awesome. I'm so happy for you. These figurines I bought yesterday remind me of family love. Tell me, what's your vision for the future? [image: a photo of a couple of wooden dolls sitting on top of a table]
Caroline (D19:3): Thanks so much, Melanie! It's beautiful! It really brings home how much love's in families - both blood and the ones we choose. I hope to build my own family and put a roof over kids who haven't had that before. For me, adoption is a way of giving back and showing love and acceptance.
Melanie (D19:4): Wow, Caroline, that's awesome. Giving a home to needy kids is such a loving way to build a family. Those kids will be so supported and happy in their new home.
Caroline (D19:5): Thanks, Melanie. My dream is to create a safe and loving home for these kids. Love and acceptance should be everyone's right, and I want them to experience it.
Melanie (D19:6): I totally agree, Caroline. Everyone deserves that. It's awesome to see how passionate you are about helping these kids.
Caroline (D19:7): Thanks, Mel. Finding self-acceptance was a long process, but now I'm ready to offer love and support to those who need it. It's empowering to make a positive difference in someone's life.
Melanie (D19:8): That must have been tough for you, Caroline. Respect for finding acceptance and helping others with what you've been through. You're so strong and inspiring.
Caroline (D19:9): Thanks, Melanie. Transitioning wasn't easy and acceptance wasn't either, but the help I got from friends, family and people I looked up to was invaluable. They boosted me through tough times and helped me find out who I really am. That's why I want to pass that same support to anyone who needs it. Bringing others comfort and helping them grow brings me such joy.
Melanie (D19:10): I'm so happy for you, Caroline. You found your true self and now you're helping others. You're so inspiring!
Caroline (D19:11): Thanks, Melanie. Your support really means a lot. This journey has been amazing and I'm grateful I get to share it and help others with theirs. It's a real gift. [image: a photo of a clock with a green and yellow design on it]
Melanie (D19:12): Absolutely! I'm so glad we can always be there for each other.

Caroline (D4:1): Hey Melanie! Long time no talk! A lot's been going on in my life! Take a look at this. [image: a photo of a person holding a necklace with a cross and a heart]

Caroline (D4:5): Yep, Melanie! I've got some other stuff with sentimental value, like my hand-painted bowl. A friend made it for my 18th birthday ten years ago. The pattern and colors are awesome-- it reminds me of art and self-expression.

Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?

Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?

Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?

Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 10:37 am on 27 June, 2023.
Session id: session_4.

Caroline (D4:1): Hey Melanie! Long time no talk! A lot's been going on in my life! Take a look at this. [image: a photo of a person holding a necklace with a cross and a heart]
Melanie (D4:2): Hey, Caroline! Nice to hear from you! Love the necklace, any special meaning to it?
Caroline (D4:3): Thanks, Melanie! This necklace is super special to me - a gift from my grandma in my home country, Sweden. She gave it to me when I was young, and it stands for love, faith and strength. It's like a reminder of my roots and all the love and support I get from my family.
Melanie (D4:4): That's gorgeous, Caroline! It's awesome what items can mean so much to us, right? Got any other objects that you treasure, like that necklace? [image: a photo of a stack of bowls with different designs on them]
Caroline (D4:5): Yep, Melanie! I've got some other stuff with sentimental value, like my hand-painted bowl. A friend made it for my 18th birthday ten years ago. The pattern and colors are awesome-- it reminds me of art and self-expression.
Melanie (D4:6): That sounds great, Caroline! It's awesome having stuff around that make us think of good connections and times. Actually, I just took my fam camping in the mountains last week - it was a really nice time together!
Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?
Melanie (D4:8): It was an awesome time, Caroline! We explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire and even went on a hike. The view from the top was amazing! The 2 younger kids love nature. It was so special having these moments together as a family - I'll never forget it!
Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?
Caroline (D4:11): Lately, I've been looking into counseling and mental health as a career. I want to help people who have gone through the same things as me. [image: a photo of a book shelf with many books on it]
Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?
Caroline (D4:13): I'm still figuring out the details, but I'm thinking of working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, I went to an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and it was really enlightening. They talked about different therapeutic methods and how to best work with trans people. Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.
Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?
Caroline (D4:15): Thanks, Melanie. It really mattered. My own journey and the support I got made a huge difference. Now I want to help people go through it too. I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Caroline (D16:1): Hey Mel, long time no chat! I had a wicked day out with the gang last weekend - we went biking and saw some pretty cool stuff. It was so refreshing, and the pic I'm sending is just stunning, eh? [image: a photo of a beach with a fence and a sunset]
Melanie (D16:2): Hey Caroline! It's so good to hear from you! That pic is so beautiful, the colors really pop. Biking sounds like a great way to get out in nature. We went camping with the kids a few weeks ago, had a blast exploring the forest and hiking. Nature can be so refreshing for your soul. Any plans coming up? [image: a photo of a dirt road surrounded by trees with yellow leaves]
Caroline (D16:3): Melanie, that photo's amazing! I love all the yellow leaves, it looks so cozy. That sounds like fun! Seeing how excited they get for the little things is awesome, it's so contagious.
Melanie (D16:4): Thanks, Caroline! It's awesome seeing the kids get excited learning something new about nature. Those moments make being a parent worth it. We roasted marshmallows and shared stories around the campfire. Those simple moments make the best memories. What inspires you with your volunteering?
Caroline (D16:5): I'm inspired seeing my work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community. Knowing I'm helping create a more loving world is amazing. I'm really thankful for my friends, family and mentors' support. It inspires me to keep making art, too. [image: a photo of a painting of a heart on a table]
Melanie (D16:6): Wow, Caroline, that looks awesome! I love how it shows the togetherness and power you were talking about. How long have you been creating art?
Caroline (D16:7): Since I was 17 or so. I find it soempowering and cathartic. It's amazing how art can show things that are hard to put into words. How long have you been into art?
Melanie (D16:8): Seven years now, and I've finally found my real muses: painting and pottery. It's so calming and satisfying. Check out my pottery creation in the pic! [image: a photo of a group of bowls and a starfish on a white surface]
Caroline (D16:9): Melanie, those bowls are amazing! They each have such cool designs. I love that you chose pottery for your art. Painting and drawing have helped me express my feelings and explore my gender identity. Creating art was really important to me during my transition - it helped me understand and accept myself. I'm so grateful.
Melanie (D16:10): Thanks, Caroline! It has really helped me out. I love how it's both a creative outlet and a form of therapy. Have you ever thought about trying it or another art form?
Caroline (D16:11): I haven't done pottery yet, but I'm game for trying new art. I might try it sometime! Check out this piece I made! [image: a photo of a painting on a easel with a red and blue background]
Melanie (D16:12): Wow, Caroline! This painting is awesome. Love the red and blue. What gave you the idea?
Caroline (D16:13): Thanks, Melanie! I made this painting to show my path as a trans woman. The red and blue are for the binary gender system, and the mix of colors means smashing that rigid thinking. It's a reminder to love my authentic self - it's taken a while to get here but I'm finally proud of who I am.
Melanie (D16:14): Wow, Caro, that painting is amazing! You've made so much progress. I'm super proud of you for being your true self. What effect has the journey had on your relationships?
Caroline (D16:15): Thanks, Melanie. It's definitely changed them. Some close friends kept supporting me, but a few weren't able to handle it. It wasn't easy, but I'm much happier being around those who accept and love me. Now my relationships feel more genuine.
Melanie (D16:16): Caroline, it's got to be tough dealing with those changes. Glad you've found people who uplift and accept you! Here's to a good time at the café last weekend - they even had thoughtful signs like this! It brings me so much happiness. [image: a photo of a sign posted on a door stating that someone is not being able to leave]
Caroline (D16:17): Whoa, Mel, that sign looks serious. Did anything happen?
Melanie (D16:18): The sign was just a precaution, I had a great time. But thank you for your concern, you're so thoughtful!
Caroline (D16:19): Phew! Glad it all worked out and you had a good time at the park!
Melanie (D16:20): Yeah, it was so much fun! Those joyful moments definitely show us life's beauty.

Caroline (D5:11): Wow, Mel, I'm so stoked for you that art is helping you express yourself and bring you joy! Keep it up!

Caroline (D5:15): Cool, thanks Mel! Can't wait. I'll keep ya posted. Bye!

Melanie (D12:2): Hey Caroline, sorry about the hike. It sucks when people are so closed-minded. Strong support really helps. FYI, I finished another pottery project - want to see a pic?

Melanie (D12:6): Thanks, Caroline! I'm obsessed with those, so I made something to catch the eye and make people smile. Plus, painting helps me express my feelings and be creative. Each stroke carries a part of me.
Caroline (D12:7): That's amazing! You put so much effort and passion into it. Your creativity really shines. Seeing how art can be a source of self-expression and growth is truly inspiring. You're killing it!
Melanie (D12:8): Thanks, Caroline! Your words really mean a lot. I've always felt a strong connection to art, and it's been a huge learning experience. It's both a sanctuary and a source of comfort. I'm so glad to have something that brings me so much happiness and fulfillment.

Caroline (D6:1): Hey Mel! Long time no talk. Lots has been going on since then!

Melanie (D6:6): They were stoked for the dinosaur exhibit! They love learning about animals and the bones were so cool. It reminds me why I love being a mom.
Caroline (D6:7): Being a mom is awesome. I'm creating a library for when I have kids. I'm really looking forward to reading to them and opening up their minds. [image: a photo of a bookcase filled with books and toys]
Melanie (D6:8): Sounds great! What kind of books you got in your library?

Melanie (D6:12): That's a gorgeous photo, Caroline! Wow, the love around you is awesome. How have your friends and fam been helping you out with your transition?

Melanie (D6:14): Wow, Caroline! It's great you have people to support you, that's really awesome!
Caroline (D6:15): I'm so lucky to have such a great support system around me. Their love and encouragement has really helped me accept and grow into my true self. They've been instrumental in my transition.

Caroline (D2:14): I'm thrilled to make a family for kids who need one. It'll be tough as a single parent, but I'm up for the challenge!

Melanie (D2:17): No doubts, Caroline. You have such a caring heart - they'll get all the love and stability they need! Excited for this new chapter!

Melanie (D4:6): That sounds great, Caroline! It's awesome having stuff around that make us think of good connections and times. Actually, I just took my fam camping in the mountains last week - it was a really nice time together!

Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?

Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?

I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:36 pm on 3 July, 2023.
Session id: session_5.

Caroline (D5:1): Since we last spoke, some big things have happened. Last week I went to an LGBTQ+ pride parade. Everyone was so happy and it made me feel like I belonged. It showed me how much our community has grown, it was amazing!
Melanie (D5:2): Wow, Caroline, sounds like the parade was an awesome experience! It's great to see the love and support for the LGBTQ+ community. Congrats! Has this experience influenced your goals at all?
Caroline (D5:3): Thanks, Mel! It really motivated me for sure. Talking to the community made me want to use my story to help others too - I'm still thinking that counseling and mental health is the way to go. I'm super excited to give back.
Melanie (D5:4): Wow, Caroline! That's great! I just signed up for a pottery class yesterday. It's like therapy for me, letting me express myself and get creative. Have you found any activities that make you feel the same way? [image: a photo of a person holding a frisbee in their hand]
Caroline (D5:5): Wow, Melanie! I'm getting creative too, just learning the piano. What made you try pottery?
Melanie (D5:6): I'm a big fan of pottery - the creativity and skill is awesome. Plus, making it is so calming. Look at this! [image: a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design]
Caroline (D5:7): That bowl is gorgeous! The black and white design looks so fancy. Did you make it?
Melanie (D5:8): Thanks, Caroline! Yeah, I made this bowl in my class. It took some work, but I'm pretty proud of it.
Caroline (D5:9): Nice job! You really put in the work and it definitely shows. Your creativity looks great!
Melanie (D5:10): Thanks, Caroline! Your kind words mean a lot. Pottery is a huge part of my life, not just a hobby - it helps me express my emotions. Clay is incredible, it brings me so much joy!
Caroline (D5:11): Wow, Mel, I'm so stoked for you that art is helping you express yourself and bring you joy! Keep it up!
Melanie (D5:12): Thanks, Caroline! I'm excited to see where pottery takes me. Anything coming up you're looking forward to?
Caroline (D5:13): Thanks Mel! I'm going to a transgender conference this month. I'm so excited to meet other people in the community and learn more about advocacy. It's gonna be great!
Melanie (D5:14): Sounds awesome, Caroline! Have a great time and learn a lot. Have fun!
Caroline (D5:15): Cool, thanks Mel! Can't wait. I'll keep ya posted. Bye!
Melanie (D5:16): Bye, Caroline! Can't wait to hear about it. Have fun and stay safe!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023.
Session id: session_1.

Caroline (D1:1): Hey Mel! Good to see you! How have you been?
Melanie (D1:2): Hey Caroline! Good to see you! I'm swamped with the kids & work. What's up with you? Anything new?
Caroline (D1:3): I went to a LGBTQ support group yesterday and it was so powerful.
Melanie (D1:4): Wow, that's cool, Caroline! What happened that was so awesome? Did you hear any inspiring stories?
Caroline (D1:5): The transgender stories were so inspiring! I was so happy and thankful for all the support. [image: a photo of a dog walking past a wall with a painting of a woman]
Melanie (D1:6): Wow, love that painting! So cool you found such a helpful group. What's it done for you?
Caroline (D1:7): The support group has made me feel accepted and given me courage to embrace myself.
Melanie (D1:8): That's really cool. You've got guts. What now?
Caroline (D1:9): Gonna continue my edu and check out career options, which is pretty exciting!
Melanie (D1:10): Wow, Caroline! What kinda jobs are you thinkin' of? Anything that stands out?
Caroline (D1:11): I'm keen on counseling or working in mental health - I'd love to support those with similar issues.
Melanie (D1:12): You'd be a great counselor! Your empathy and understanding will really help the people you work with. By the way, take a look at this. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunset over a lake]
Caroline (D1:13): Thanks, Melanie! That's really sweet. Is this your own painting?
Melanie (D1:14): Yeah, I painted that lake sunrise last year! It's special to me.
Caroline (D1:15): Wow, Melanie! The colors really blend nicely. Painting looks like a great outlet for expressing yourself.
Melanie (D1:16): Thanks, Caroline! Painting's a fun way to express my feelings and get creative. It's a great way to relax after a long day.
Caroline (D1:17): Totally agree, Mel. Relaxing and expressing ourselves is key. Well, I'm off to go do some research.
Melanie (D1:18): Yep, Caroline. Taking care of ourselves is vital. I'm off to go swimming with the kids. Talk to you soon!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 10:37 am on 27 June, 2023.
Session id: session_4.

Caroline (D4:1): Hey Melanie! Long time no talk! A lot's been going on in my life! Take a look at this. [image: a photo of a person holding a necklace with a cross and a heart]
Melanie (D4:2): Hey, Caroline! Nice to hear from you! Love the necklace, any special meaning to it?
Caroline (D4:3): Thanks, Melanie! This necklace is super special to me - a gift from my grandma in my home country, Sweden. She gave it to me when I was young, and it stands for love, faith and strength. It's like a reminder of my roots and all the love and support I get from my family.
Melanie (D4:4): That's gorgeous, Caroline! It's awesome what items can mean so much to us, right? Got any other objects that you treasure, like that necklace? [image: a photo of a stack of bowls with different designs on them]
Caroline (D4:5): Yep, Melanie! I've got some other stuff with sentimental value, like my hand-painted bowl. A friend made it for my 18th birthday ten years ago. The pattern and colors are awesome-- it reminds me of art and self-expression.
Melanie (D4:6): That sounds great, Caroline! It's awesome having stuff around that make us think of good connections and times. Actually, I just took my fam camping in the mountains last week - it was a really nice time together!
Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?
Melanie (D4:8): It was an awesome time, Caroline! We explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire and even went on a hike. The view from the top was amazing! The 2 younger kids love nature. It was so special having these moments together as a family - I'll never forget it!
Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?
Caroline (D4:11): Lately, I've been looking into counseling and mental health as a career. I want to help people who have gone through the same things as me. [image: a photo of a book shelf with many books on it]
Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?
Caroline (D4:13): I'm still figuring out the details, but I'm thinking of working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, I went to an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and it was really enlightening. They talked about different therapeutic methods and how to best work with trans people. Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.
Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?
Caroline (D4:15): Thanks, Melanie. It really mattered. My own journey and the support I got made a huge difference. Now I want to help people go through it too. I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 2:31 pm on 17 July, 2023.
Session id: session_9.

Melanie (D9:1): Hey Caroline, hope all's good! I had a quiet weekend after we went camping with my fam two weekends ago. It was great to unplug and hang with the kids. What've you been up to? Anything fun over the weekend?
Caroline (D9:2): Hey Melanie! That sounds great! Last weekend I joined a mentorship program for LGBTQ youth - it's really rewarding to help the community.
Melanie (D9:3): Wow, Caroline! It's great that you're helping out. How's it going? Got any cool experiences you can share?
Caroline (D9:4): The mentoring is going great! I've met some amazing young folks and supported them along the way. It's inspiring to see how resilient and strong they are.
Melanie (D9:5): Wow, Caroline, that sounds super rewarding! Young people's resilience is amazing. Care to share some stories?
Caroline (D9:6): I mentor a transgender teen just like me. We've been working on building up confidence and finding positive strategies, and it's really been paying off! We had a great time at the LGBT pride event last month.
Melanie (D9:7): Caroline, awesome news that you two are getting along! What was it like for you both? Care to fill me in?
Caroline (D9:8): The pride event was awesome! It was so encouraging to be surrounded by so much love and acceptance. [image: a photo of a woman holding a rainbow umbrella in the air]
Melanie (D9:9): Wow! What's the best part you remember from it?
Caroline (D9:10): Seeing my mentee's face light up when they saw the support was the best! Such a special moment.
Melanie (D9:11): Wow, Caroline! They must have felt so appreciated. It's awesome to see the difference we can make in each other's lives. Any other exciting LGBTQ advocacy stuff coming up?
Caroline (D9:12): Yay! Next month I'm having an LGBTQ art show with my paintings - can't wait!
Melanie (D9:13): Wow, Caroline, that sounds awesome! Can't wait to see your art - got any previews? [image: a photo of a painting with a blue and yellow design]
Caroline (D9:14): Check out my painting for the art show! Hope you like it. [image: a photography of a painting of a tree with a bright sun in the background]
Melanie (D9:15): Wow, Caroline, that painting is awesome! Those colors are so vivid and the whole thing looks really unified. What inspired you?
Caroline (D9:16): Thanks, Melanie! I painted this after I visited a LGBTQ center. I wanted to capture everyone's unity and strength.
Melanie (D9:17): Wow, Caroline! It really conveys unity and strength - such a gorgeous piece! My kids and I just finished another painting like our last one.

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:14 pm on 25 May, 2023.
Session id: session_2.

Melanie (D2:1): Hey Caroline, since we last chatted, I've had a lot of things happening to me. I ran a charity race for mental health last Saturday – it was really rewarding. Really made me think about taking care of our minds.
Caroline (D2:2): That charity race sounds great, Mel! Making a difference & raising awareness for mental health is super rewarding - I'm really proud of you for taking part!
Melanie (D2:3): Thanks, Caroline! The event was really thought-provoking. I'm starting to realize that self-care is really important. It's a journey for me, but when I look after myself, I'm able to better look after my family.
Caroline (D2:4): I totally agree, Melanie. Taking care of ourselves is so important - even if it's not always easy. Great that you're prioritizing self-care.
Melanie (D2:5): Yeah, it's tough. So I'm carving out some me-time each day - running, reading, or playing my violin - which refreshes me and helps me stay present for my fam!
Caroline (D2:6): That's great, Mel! Taking time for yourself is so important. You're doing an awesome job looking after yourself and your family!
Melanie (D2:7): Thanks, Caroline. It's still a work in progress, but I'm doing my best. My kids are so excited about summer break! We're thinking about going camping next month. Any fun plans for the summer?
Caroline (D2:8): Researching adoption agencies — it's been a dream to have a family and give a loving home to kids who need it.
Melanie (D2:9): Wow, Caroline! That's awesome! Taking in kids in need - you're so kind. Your future family is gonna be so lucky to have you!
Caroline (D2:10): Thanks, Mel! My goal is to give kids a loving home. I'm truly grateful for all the support I've got from friends and mentors. Now the hard work starts to turn my dream into a reality. And here's one of the adoption agencies I'm looking into. It's a lot to take in, but I'm feeling hopeful and optimistic. [image: a photography of a sign for a new arrival and an information and domestic building]
Melanie (D2:11): Wow, that agency looks great! What made you pick it?
Caroline (D2:12): I chose them 'cause they help LGBTQ+ folks with adoption. Their inclusivity and support really spoke to me.
Melanie (D2:13): That's great, Caroline! Loving the inclusivity and support. Anything you're excited for in the adoption process?
Caroline (D2:14): I'm thrilled to make a family for kids who need one. It'll be tough as a single parent, but I'm up for the challenge!
Melanie (D2:15): You're doing something amazing! Creating a family for those kids is so lovely. You'll be an awesome mom! Good luck!
Caroline (D2:16): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words really mean a lot. I'll do my best to make sure these kids have a safe and loving home.
Melanie (D2:17): No doubts, Caroline. You have such a caring heart - they'll get all the love and stability they need! Excited for this new chapter!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 2:24 pm on 14 August, 2023.
Session id: session_11.

Melanie (D11:1): Hey Caroline! Last night was amazing! We celebrated my daughter's birthday with a concert surrounded by music, joy and the warm summer breeze. Seeing my kids' smiles was so awesome, and I'm so thankful for our special moments together.
Caroline (D11:2): Wow, sounds wonderful! Your love for your kids is so awesome. What concert was it? The advocacy event was a cool experience - so much love and support, amazing! [image: a photo of a poster for a concert with a picture of a man]
Melanie (D11:3): Thanks, Caroline! It was Matt Patterson, he is so talented! His voice and songs were amazing. What's up with you? Anything interesting going on?
Caroline (D11:4): Wow, Mel, glad you had a blast at the concert. A lot's happened since we talked. I went to a pride parade last Friday and it was awesome - so much energy and love everywhere. Really made me proud and reminded me how important it is to keep standing up for equality.
Melanie (D11:5): Wow, that's awesome! How did it feel being part of that community? [image: a photo of a band performing on stage with a sign that says all are welcome]
Caroline (D11:6): It was so inspiring, Mel! Check out the crowd. People of all kinds celebrating love and acceptance - it really pushed me to keep fighting for LGBTQ rights. [image: a photo of a group of people walking down a street with balloons]
Melanie (D11:7): Wow, Caroline! That sounds awesome. This pic's from last night - looks like everyone was having a blast! Reminds me it's important to cultivate a loving and accepting environment for our kids. How do you stay inclusive in your work as an artist? [image: a photo of a group of people sitting on chairs watching a band]
Caroline (D11:8): That pic is cool! Representing inclusivity and diversity in my art is important to me. I also use it to speak up for the LGBTQ+ community and push for acceptance. Here's a recent painting! [image: a photo of a painting with a painting brush and paint on it]
Melanie (D11:9): Wow, that rocks! What's the main idea of your art?
Caroline (D11:10): My art is about expressing my trans experience. It's my way of showing my story and helping people understand the trans community. [image: a photo of a painting of a woman with a cow in her lap]
Melanie (D11:11): Your art's amazing, Caroline. I love how you use it to tell your stories and teach people about trans folks. I'd love to see another painting of yours! [image: a photo of a person holding a purple bowl in their hand]
Caroline (D11:12): Thanks, Melanie. Here's one- 'Embracing Identity' is all about finding comfort and love in being yourself. The woman in the painting stands for the journey of acceptance. My aim was to show warmth, love and self-acceptance. [image: a photo of a painting of a woman with a red shirt]
Melanie (D11:13): Wow, Caroline, that's gorgeous! I love the self-acceptance and love theme. How does art help you with your self-discovery and acceptance journey? [image: a photo of a woman is making a vase on a wheel]
Caroline (D11:14): Art's allowed me to explore my transition and my changing body. It's been a great way to work through stuff I'm going through. I love that it teaches me to accept the beauty of imperfections.
Melanie (D11:15): Wow, Caroline, that's so cool! Art can be so healing and a way to really connect with who you are. It's awesome that beauty can be found in the imperfections. We're all individual and wonderfully imperfect. Thanks for sharing it with me!
Caroline (D11:16): Thanks, Melanie. It means a lot to share this with you.
Melanie (D11:17): Great chatting with you! Feel free to reach out any time.

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:50 pm on 17 August, 2023.
Session id: session_12.

Caroline (D12:1): Hey Mel! How're ya doin'? Recently, I had a not-so-great experience on a hike. I ran into a group of religious conservatives who said something that really upset me. It made me think how much work we still have to do for LGBTQ rights. It's been so helpful to have people around me who accept and support me, so I know I'll be ok!
Melanie (D12:2): Hey Caroline, sorry about the hike. It sucks when people are so closed-minded. Strong support really helps. FYI, I finished another pottery project - want to see a pic?
Caroline (D12:3): Sure thing, Melanie! Can't wait to see your pottery project.  I'm happy you found something that makes you happy. Show me when you can!
Melanie (D12:4): Here it is. Pretty proud of it! It was a great experience. Thoughts? [image: a photo of a bowl with a colorful design on it]
Caroline (D12:5): That bowl is awesome, Mel! What gave you the idea for all the colors and patterns?
Melanie (D12:6): Thanks, Caroline! I'm obsessed with those, so I made something to catch the eye and make people smile. Plus, painting helps me express my feelings and be creative. Each stroke carries a part of me.
Caroline (D12:7): That's amazing! You put so much effort and passion into it. Your creativity really shines. Seeing how art can be a source of self-expression and growth is truly inspiring. You're killing it!
Melanie (D12:8): Thanks, Caroline! Your words really mean a lot. I've always felt a strong connection to art, and it's been a huge learning experience. It's both a sanctuary and a source of comfort. I'm so glad to have something that brings me so much happiness and fulfillment.
Caroline (D12:9): Glad you found something that makes you so happy! Surrounding ourselves with things that bring us joy is important. Life's too short to do anything else!
Melanie (D12:10): Agreed, Caroline. Life's tough but it's worth it when we have things that make us happy.
Caroline (D12:11): Definitely, Mel! Finding those happy moments and clinging to them is key. It's what keeps us going, even when life's hard. I'm lucky to have people like you to remind me.
Melanie (D12:12): Yeah, same here Caroline. You make life's struggles more bearable.
Caroline (D12:13): Thanks, Melanie! It means a lot having you in my corner. Appreciate our friendship!
Melanie (D12:14): I appreciate our friendship too, Caroline. You've always been there for me.
Caroline (D12:15): I'm always here for you, Mel! We had a blast last year at the Pride fest. Those supportive friends definitely make everything worth it! [image: a photo of a group of people walking down a street with balloons]
Melanie (D12:16): That was a blast! So much fun with the whole gang! Wanna do a family outing this summer?
Caroline (D12:17): Right, it was so much fun! We could do a family outting, or wanna plan something special for this summer, just us two? It'd be a great chance to catch up and explore nature! What do you think?
Melanie (D12:18): Sounds great, Caroline! Let's plan something special!
Caroline (D12:19): Sounds great, Mel! We'll make some awesome memories!
Melanie (D12:20): Yeah, Caroline! I'll start thinking about what we can do.
Caroline (D12:21): Yeah, Mel! Life's all about creating memories. Can't wait for the trip!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:33 pm on 25 August, 2023.
Session id: session_14.

Caroline (D14:1): Hey, Mel! How's it going? There's something I want to tell you. I went hiking last week and got into a bad spot with some people. It really bugged me, so I tried to apologize to them. [image: a photo of a woman sitting on a sign on top of a mountain]
Melanie (D14:2): Wow, Caroline! Sorry that happened to you. It's tough when those things happen, but it's great you apologized. Takes a lot of courage and maturity! What do you think of this? [image: a photo of a plate with a bunch of flowers on it]
Caroline (D14:3): Thanks, Melanie! That plate is awesome! Did you make it?
Melanie (D14:4): Yeah, I made it in pottery class yesterday. I love it! Pottery's so relaxing and creative. Have you tried it yet?
Caroline (D14:5): Nah, I haven't. I've been busy painting - here's something I just finished. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunset on a small easel]
Melanie (D14:6): Wow Caroline, that looks amazing! Those colors are so vivid, it really looks like a real sunset. What gave you the idea to paint it?
Caroline (D14:7): Thanks, Melanie! I painted it after I visited the beach last week. Just seeing the sun dip below the horizon, all the amazing colors - it was amazing and calming. So I just had to try to capture that feeling in my painting. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunset over the ocean]
Melanie (D14:8): Wow, the beach really inspired you. The art really took me to that moment and I can feel the serenity. You captured the sunset perfectly, so peaceful!
Caroline (D14:9): Thanks Mel, really appreciate your kind words. It means a lot to me that you can feel the sense of peace and serenity. Makes me feel connected.
Melanie (D14:10): I feel the same way! Art is so cool like that - it connects us and helps us understand each other. I was actually just remembering yesterday, spending the day with my fam volunteering at a homeless shelter. It was hard to see how neglected some people are, but it was great to feel like we could make a difference.

Melanie (D11:3): Thanks, Caroline! It was Matt Patterson, he is so talented! His voice and songs were amazing. What's up with you? Anything interesting going on?
Caroline (D11:4): Wow, Mel, glad you had a blast at the concert. A lot's happened since we talked. I went to a pride parade last Friday and it was awesome - so much energy and love everywhere. Really made me proud and reminded me how important it is to keep standing up for equality.
Melanie (D11:5): Wow, that's awesome! How did it feel being part of that community? [image: a photo of a band performing on stage with a sign that says all are welcome]
Caroline (D11:6): It was so inspiring, Mel! Check out the crowd. People of all kinds celebrating love and acceptance - it really pushed me to keep fighting for LGBTQ rights. [image: a photo of a group of people walking down a street with balloons]
Melanie (D11:7): Wow, Caroline! That sounds awesome. This pic's from last night - looks like everyone was having a blast! Reminds me it's important to cultivate a loving and accepting environment for our kids. How do you stay inclusive in your work

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 10:37 am on 27 June, 2023.
Session id: session_4.

Caroline (D4:1): Hey Melanie! Long time no talk! A lot's been going on in my life! Take a look at this. [image: a photo of a person holding a necklace with a cross and a heart]
Melanie (D4:2): Hey, Caroline! Nice to hear from you! Love the necklace, any special meaning to it?
Caroline (D4:3): Thanks, Melanie! This necklace is super special to me - a gift from my grandma in my home country, Sweden. She gave it to me when I was young, and it stands for love, faith and strength. It's like a reminder of my roots and all the love and support I get from my family.
Melanie (D4:4): That's gorgeous, Caroline! It's awesome what items can mean so much to us, right? Got any other objects that you treasure, like that necklace? [image: a photo of a stack of bowls with different designs on them]
Caroline (D4:5): Yep, Melanie! I've got some other stuff with sentimental value, like my hand-painted bowl. A friend made it for my 18th birthday ten years ago. The pattern and colors are awesome-- it reminds me of art and self-expression.
Melanie (D4:6): That sounds great, Caroline! It's awesome having stuff around that make us think of good connections and times. Actually, I just took my fam camping in the mountains last week - it was a really nice time together!
Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?
Melanie (D4:8): It was an awesome time, Caroline! We explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire and even went on a hike. The view from the top was amazing! The 2 younger kids love nature. It was so special having these moments together as a family - I'll never forget it!
Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?
Caroline (D4:11): Lately, I've been looking into counseling and mental health as a career. I want to help people who have gone through the same things as me. [image: a photo of a book shelf with many books on it]
Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?
Caroline (D4:13): I'm still figuring out the details, but I'm thinking of working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, I went to an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and it was really enlightening. They talked about different therapeutic methods and how to best work with trans people. Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.
Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?
Caroline (D4:15): Thanks, Melanie. It really mattered. My own journey and the support I got made a huge difference. Now I want to help people go through it too. I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:36 pm on 3 July, 2023.
Session id: session_5.

Caroline (D5:1): Since we last spoke, some big things have happened. Last week I went to an LGBTQ+ pride parade. Everyone was so happy and it made me feel like I belonged. It showed me how much our community has grown, it was amazing!
Melanie (D5:2): Wow, Caroline, sounds like the parade was an awesome experience! It's great to see the love and support for the LGBTQ+ community. Congrats! Has this experience influenced your goals at all?
Caroline (D5:3): Thanks, Mel! It really motivated me for sure. Talking to the community made me want to use my story to help others too - I'm still thinking that counseling and mental health is the way to go. I'm super excited to give back.
Melanie (D5:4): Wow, Caroline! That's great! I just signed up for a pottery class yesterday. It's like therapy for me, letting me express myself and get creative. Have you found any activities that make you feel the same way? [image: a photo of a person holding a frisbee in their hand]
Caroline (D5:5): Wow, Melanie! I'm getting creative too, just learning the piano. What made you try pottery?
Melanie (D5:6): I'm a big fan of pottery - the creativity and skill is awesome. Plus, making it is so calming. Look at this! [image: a photo of a bowl with a black and white flower design]
Caroline (D5:7): That bowl is gorgeous! The black and white design looks so fancy. Did you make it?
Melanie (D5:8): Thanks, Caroline! Yeah, I made this bowl in my class. It took some work, but I'm pretty proud of it.
Caroline (D5:9): Nice job! You really put in the work and it definitely shows. Your creativity looks great!
Melanie (D5:10): Thanks, Caroline! Your kind words mean a lot. Pottery is a huge part of my life, not just a hobby - it helps me express my emotions. Clay is incredible, it brings me so much joy!
Caroline (D5:11): Wow, Mel, I'm so stoked for you that art is helping you express yourself and bring you joy! Keep it up!
Melanie (D5:12): Thanks, Caroline! I'm excited to see where pottery takes me. Anything coming up you're looking forward to?
Caroline (D5:13): Thanks Mel! I'm going to a transgender conference this month. I'm so excited to meet other people in the community and learn more about advocacy. It's gonna be great!
Melanie (D5:14): Sounds awesome, Caroline! Have a great time and learn a lot. Have fun!
Caroline (D5:15): Cool, thanks Mel! Can't wait. I'll keep ya posted. Bye!
Melanie (D5:16): Bye, Caroline! Can't wait to hear about it. Have fun and stay safe!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:50 pm on 17 August, 2023.
Session id: session_12.

Caroline (D12:1): Hey Mel! How're ya doin'? Recently, I had a not-so-great experience on a hike. I ran into a group of religious conservatives who said something that really upset me. It made me think how much work we still have to do for LGBTQ rights. It's been so helpful to have people around me who accept and support me, so I know I'll be ok!
Melanie (D12:2): Hey Caroline, sorry about the hike. It sucks when people are so closed-minded. Strong support really helps. FYI, I finished another pottery project - want to see a pic?
Caroline (D12:3): Sure thing, Melanie! Can't wait to see your pottery project.  I'm happy you found something that makes you happy. Show me when you can!
Melanie (D12:4): Here it is. Pretty proud of it! It was a great experience. Thoughts? [image: a photo of a bowl with a colorful design on it]
Caroline (D12:5): That bowl is awesome, Mel! What gave you the idea for all the colors and patterns?
Melanie (D12:6): Thanks, Caroline! I'm obsessed with those, so I made something to catch the eye and make people smile. Plus, painting helps me express my feelings and be creative. Each stroke carries a part of me.
Caroline (D12:7): That's amazing! You put so much effort and passion into it. Your creativity really shines. Seeing how art can be a source of self-expression and growth is truly inspiring. You're killing it!
Melanie (D12:8): Thanks, Caroline! Your words really mean a lot. I've always felt a strong connection to art, and it's been a huge learning experience. It's both a sanctuary and a source of comfort. I'm so glad to have something that brings me so much happiness and fulfillment.
Caroline (D12:9): Glad you found something that makes you so happy! Surrounding ourselves with things that bring us joy is important. Life's too short to do anything else!
Melanie (D12:10): Agreed, Caroline. Life's tough but it's worth it when we have things that make us happy.
Caroline (D12:11): Definitely, Mel! Finding those happy moments and clinging to them is key. It's what keeps us going, even when life's hard. I'm lucky to have people like you to remind me.
Melanie (D12:12): Yeah, same here Caroline. You make life's struggles more bearable.
Caroline (D12:13): Thanks, Melanie! It means a lot having you in my corner. Appreciate our friendship!
Melanie (D12:14): I appreciate our friendship too, Caroline. You've always been there for me.
Caroline (D12:15): I'm always here for you, Mel! We had a blast last year at the Pride fest. Those supportive friends definitely make everything worth it! [image: a photo of a group of people walking down a street with balloons]
Melanie (D12:16): That was a blast! So much fun with the whole gang! Wanna do a family outing this summer?
Caroline (D12:17): Right, it was so much fun! We could do a family outting, or wanna plan something special for this summer, just us two? It'd be a great chance to catch up and explore nature! What do you think?
Melanie (D12:18): Sounds great, Caroline! Let's plan something special!
Caroline (D12:19): Sounds great, Mel! We'll make some awesome memories!
Melanie (D12:20): Yeah, Caroline! I'll start thinking about what we can do.
Caroline (D12:21): Yeah, Mel! Life's all about creating memories. Can't wait for the trip!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:14 pm on 25 May, 2023.
Session id: session_2.

Melanie (D2:1): Hey Caroline, since we last chatted, I've had a lot of things happening to me. I ran a charity race for mental health last Saturday – it was really rewarding. Really made me think about taking care of our minds.
Caroline (D2:2): That charity race sounds great, Mel! Making a difference & raising awareness for mental health is super rewarding - I'm really proud of you for taking part!
Melanie (D2:3): Thanks, Caroline! The event was really thought-provoking. I'm starting to realize that self-care is really important. It's a journey for me, but when I look after myself, I'm able to better look after my family.
Caroline (D2:4): I totally agree, Melanie. Taking care of ourselves is so important - even if it's not always easy. Great that you're prioritizing self-care.
Melanie (D2:5): Yeah, it's tough. So I'm carving out some me-time each day - running, reading, or playing my violin - which refreshes me and helps me stay present for my fam!
Caroline (D2:6): That's great, Mel! Taking time for yourself is so important. You're doing an awesome job looking after yourself and your family!
Melanie (D2:7): Thanks, Caroline. It's still a work in progress, but I'm doing my best. My kids are so excited about summer break! We're thinking about going camping next month. Any fun plans for the summer?
Caroline (D2:8): Researching adoption agencies — it's been a dream to have a family and give a loving home to kids who need it.
Melanie (D2:9): Wow, Caroline! That's awesome! Taking in kids in need - you're so kind. Your future family is gonna be so lucky to have you!
Caroline (D2:10): Thanks, Mel! My goal is to give kids a loving home. I'm truly grateful for all the support I've got from friends and mentors. Now the hard work starts to turn my dream into a reality. And here's one of the adoption agencies I'm looking into. It's a lot to take in, but I'm feeling hopeful and optimistic. [image: a photography of a sign for a new arrival and an information and domestic building]
Melanie (D2:11): Wow, that agency looks great! What made you pick it?
Caroline (D2:12): I chose them 'cause they help LGBTQ+ folks with adoption. Their inclusivity and support really spoke to me.
Melanie (D2:13): That's great, Caroline! Loving the inclusivity and support. Anything you're excited for in the adoption process?
Caroline (D2:14): I'm thrilled to make a family for kids who need one. It'll be tough as a single parent, but I'm up for the challenge!
Melanie (D2:15): You're doing something amazing! Creating a family for those kids is so lovely. You'll be an awesome mom! Good luck!
Caroline (D2:16): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words really mean a lot. I'll do my best to make sure these kids have a safe and loving home.
Melanie (D2:17): No doubts, Caroline. You have such a caring heart - they'll get all the love and stability they need! Excited for this new chapter!

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 1:33 pm on 25 August, 2023.
Session id: session_14.

Caroline (D14:1): Hey, Mel! How's it going? There's something I want to tell you. I went hiking last week and got into a bad spot with some people. It really bugged me, so I tried to apologize to them. [image: a photo of a woman sitting on a sign on top of a mountain]
Melanie (D14:2): Wow, Caroline! Sorry that happened to you. It's tough when those things happen, but it's great you apologized. Takes a lot of courage and maturity! What do you think of this? [image: a photo of a plate with a bunch of flowers on it]
Caroline (D14:3): Thanks, Melanie! That plate is awesome! Did you make it?
Melanie (D14:4): Yeah, I made it in pottery class yesterday. I love it! Pottery's so relaxing and creative. Have you tried it yet?
Caroline (D14:5): Nah, I haven't. I've been busy painting - here's something I just finished. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunset on a small easel]
Melanie (D14:6): Wow Caroline, that looks amazing! Those colors are so vivid, it really looks like a real sunset. What gave you the idea to paint it?
Caroline (D14:7): Thanks, Melanie! I painted it after I visited the beach last week. Just seeing the sun dip below the horizon, all the amazing colors - it was amazing and calming. So I just had to try to capture that feeling in my painting. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunset over the ocean]
Melanie (D14:8): Wow, the beach really inspired you. The art really took me to that moment and I can feel the serenity. You captured the sunset perfectly, so peaceful!
Caroline (D14:9): Thanks Mel, really appreciate your kind words. It means a lot to me that you can feel the sense of peace and serenity. Makes me feel connected.
Melanie (D14:10): I feel the same way! Art is so cool like that - it connects us and helps us understand each other. I was actually just remembering yesterday, spending the day with my fam volunteering at a homeless shelter. It was hard to see how neglected some people are, but it was great to feel like we could make a difference.
Caroline (D14:11): Wow, Mel, you're amazing! Volunteering and making a difference- it's so heartwarming. You're an inspiration to us all! [image: a photo of a crowd of people walking down a street with a rainbow flag]
Melanie (D14:12): Thanks, Caroline! I really appreciate your help and motivation. What made you decide to transition and join the transgender community? [image: a photo of a bulletin board with a rainbow flag and a don't ever be afraid to]
Caroline (D14:13): Finding a community where I'm accepted, loved and supported has really meant a lot to me. It's made a huge difference to have people who get what I'm going through. Stuff like this mural are really special to me! [image: a photo of a building with a large eagle painted on it]
Melanie (D14:14): Caroline, glad you found a supportive community! Can you tell me more about why it's special to you?
Caroline (D14:15): The rainbow flag mural is important to me as it reflects the courage and strength of the trans community. The eagle symbolizes freedom and pride, representing my own resilience and that of others. [image: a photo of a stained glass window with a picture of a person on a horse]
Melanie (D14:16): I'm in awe of your courage as a trans person. Have you made any more art lately? [image: a photo of a stained glass window with a person holding a key]
Caroline (D14:17): Thanks, Mel! I made this stained glass window to remind myself and others that within us all is the key to discovering our true potential and living our best life. [image: a photo of three stained glass windows in a church with a clock]
Melanie (D14:18): Wow, Caroline, that looks amazing! What inspired it?
Caroline (D14:19): Thanks! It was made for a local church and shows time changing our lives. I made it to show my own journey as a transgender woman and how we should accept growth and change. [image: a photo of a large stained glass window in a church]
Melanie (D14:20): Wow, Caroline!  All those colors are incredible and the story it tells is so inspiring. [image: a photo of a door with a stained glass window and a coat rack]
Caroline (D14:21): Thanks, Mel! Glad you like it. It's a symbol of togetherness, to celebrate differences and be that much closer. I'd love to make something like this next! [image: a photo of a painted sidewalk with a rainbow design on it]
Melanie (D14:22): Wow, that's gorgeous! Where did you find it?
Caroline (D14:23): I was out walking in my neighborhood when I came across this cool rainbow sidewalk for Pride Month. It was so vibrant and welcoming, I had to take a picture! It reminds us that love and acceptance are everywhere—even where we least expect it.
Melanie (D14:24): That's so nice, Caroline! Art can be in the most unlikely places. Love and acceptance really can be found everywhere. [image: a photo of a person drawing a flower on the ground]
Caroline (D14:25): Agreed, Mel! Art can be a real mood-booster - I saw someone drawing on the ground the other day and it made me so happy. Creativity sure can lighten someone's day. [image: a photo of a painting of flowers and a watercolor palette]
Melanie (D14:26): Wow, Caroline, that's so nice! The colors are so bright and the flowers are so pretty. Art is such a source of joy.
Caroline (D14:27): Thanks, Mel! Art gives me so much joy. It helps me show my feelings and freeze gorgeous moments, like a bouquet of flowers. [image: a photo of a drawing of a bunch of flowers on a table]
Melanie (D14:28): Wow, did you make that? It looks so real!
Caroline (D14:29): Yeah, definitely! Drawing flowers is one of my faves. Appreciating nature and sharing it is great. What about you, Mel? What type of art do you love? [image: a photo of a drawing of a flower bouquet with a person holding it]
Melanie (D14:30): Painting landscapes and still life is my favorite! Nature's amazing, here's a painting I did recently. [image: a photo of a painting of a sunflower on a canvas]
Caroline (D14:31): Wow, Mel! Any more paintings coming up?
Melanie (D14:32): I'm feeling inspired by autumn so I'm planning a few. You got any cool art projects coming up?
Caroline (D14:33): I'm putting together an LGBTQ art show next month and I'm gonna show my paintings. Super stoked!
Melanie (D14:34): Wow, Caroline, that's awesome! Can't wait to see your show - the LGBTQ community needs more platforms like this!
Caroline (D14:35): Yeah Mel, stoked! Gonna be a great night featuring LGBTQ artists and their awesome talents. We want it to spread understanding and acceptance - let's make it happen! [image: a photo of a poster for a concert with a man in a cowboy hat]

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 12:09 am on 13 September, 2023.
Session id: session_16.

Caroline (D16:1): Hey Mel, long time no chat! I had a wicked day out with the gang last weekend - we went biking and saw some pretty cool stuff. It was so refreshing, and the pic I'm sending is just stunning, eh? [image: a photo of a beach with a fence and a sunset]
Melanie (D16:2): Hey Caroline! It's so good to hear from you! That pic is so beautiful, the colors really pop. Biking sounds like a great way to get out in nature. We went camping with the kids a few weeks ago, had a blast exploring the forest and hiking. Nature can be so refreshing for your soul. Any plans coming up? [image: a photo of a dirt road surrounded by trees with yellow leaves]
Caroline (D16:3): Melanie, that photo's amazing! I love all the yellow leaves, it looks so cozy. That sounds like fun! Seeing how excited they get for the little things is awesome, it's so contagious.
Melanie (D16:4): Thanks, Caroline! It's awesome seeing the kids get excited learning something new about nature. Those moments make being a parent worth it. We roasted marshmallows and shared stories around the campfire. Those simple moments make the best memories. What inspires you with your volunteering?
Caroline (D16:5): I'm inspired seeing my work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community. Knowing I'm helping create a more loving world is amazing. I'm really thankful for my friends, family and mentors' support. It inspires me to keep making art, too. [image: a photo of a painting of a heart on a table]
Melanie (D16:6): Wow, Caroline, that looks awesome! I love how it shows the togetherness and power you were talking about. How long have you been creating art?
Caroline (D16:7): Since I was 17 or so. I find it soempowering and cathartic. It's amazing how art can show things that are hard to put into words. How long have you been into art?
Melanie (D16:8): Seven years now, and I've finally found my real muses: painting and pottery. It's so calming and satisfying. Check out my pottery creation in the pic! [image: a photo of a group of bowls and a starfish on a white surface]
Caroline (D16:9): Melanie, those bowls are amazing! They each have such cool designs. I love that you chose pottery for your art. Painting and drawing have helped me express my feelings and explore my gender identity. Creating art was really important to me during my transition - it helped me understand and accept myself. I'm so grateful.
Melanie (D16:10): Thanks, Caroline! It has really helped me out. I love how it's both a creative outlet and a form of therapy. Have you ever thought about trying it or another art form?
Caroline (D16:11): I haven't done pottery yet, but I'm game for trying new art. I might try it sometime! Check out this piece I made! [image: a photo of a painting on a easel with a red and blue background]
Melanie (D16:12): Wow, Caroline! This painting is awesome. Love the red and blue. What gave you the idea?
Caroline (D16:13): Thanks, Melanie! I made this painting to show my path as a trans woman. The red and blue are for the binary gender system, and the mix of colors means smashing that rigid thinking. It's a reminder to love my authentic self - it's taken a while to get here but I'm finally proud of who I am.
Melanie (D16:14): Wow, Caro, that painting is amazing! You've made so much progress. I'm super proud of you for being your true self. What effect has the journey had on your relationships?
Caroline (D16:15): Thanks, Melanie. It's definitely changed them. Some close friends kept supporting me, but a few weren't able to handle it. It wasn't easy, but I'm much happier being around those who accept and love me. Now my relationships feel more genuine.
Melanie (D16:16): Caroline, it's got to be tough dealing with those changes. Glad you've found people who uplift and accept you! Here's to a good time at the café last weekend - they even had thoughtful signs like this! It brings me so much happiness. [image: a photo of a sign posted on a door stating that someone is not being able to leave]
Caroline (D16:17): Whoa, Mel, that sign looks serious. Did anything happen?
Melanie (D16:18): The sign was just a precaution, I had a great time. But thank you for your concern, you're so thoughtful!
Caroline (D16:19): Phew! Glad it all worked out and you had a good time at the park!
Melanie (D16:20): Yeah, it was so much fun! Those joyful moments definitely show us life's beauty.

Conversation between Caroline and Melanie.
Session time: 8:18 pm on 6 July, 2023.
Session id: session_6.

Caroline (D6:1): Hey Mel! Long time no talk. Lots has been going on since then!

Caroline (D5:1): Since we last spoke, some big things have happened. Last week I went to an LGBTQ+ pride parade. Everyone was so happy and it made me feel like I belonged. It showed me how much our community has grown, it was amazing!

Caroline (D5:3): Thanks, Mel! It really motivated me for sure. Talking to the community made me want to use my story to help others too - I'm still thinking that counseling and mental health is the way to go. I'm super excited to give back.

Caroline (D5:11): Wow, Mel, I'm so stoked for you that art is helping you express yourself and bring you joy! Keep it up!
Melanie (D5:12): Thanks, Caroline! I'm excited to see where pottery takes me. Anything coming up you're looking forward to?
Caroline (D5:13): Thanks Mel! I'm going to a transgender conference this month. I'm so excited to meet other people in the community and learn more about advocacy. It's gonna be great!

Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?
Melanie (D4:8): It was an awesome time, Caroline! We explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire and even went on a hike. The view from the top was amazing! The 2 younger kids love nature. It was so special having these moments together as a family - I'll never forget it!
Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?
Caroline (D4:11): Lately, I've been looking into counseling and mental health as a career. I want to help people who have gone through the same things as me. [image: a photo of a book shelf with many books on it]
Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?
Caroline (D4:13): I'm still figuring out the details, but I'm thinking of working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, I went to an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and it was really enlightening. They talked about different therapeutic methods and how to best work with trans people. Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.
Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?
Caroline (D4:15): Thanks, Melanie. It really mattered. My own journey and the support I got made a huge difference. Now I want to help people go through it too. I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Caroline (D4:1): Hey Melanie! Long time no talk! A lot's been going on in my life! Take a look at this. [image: a photo of a person holding a necklace with a cross and a heart]
Melanie (D4:2): Hey, Caroline! Nice to hear from you! Love the necklace, any special meaning to it?
Caroline (D4:3): Thanks, Melanie! This necklace is super special to me - a gift from my grandma in my home country, Sweden. She gave it to me when I was young, and it stands for love, faith and strength. It's like a reminder of my roots and all the love and support I get from my family.
Melanie (D4:4): That's gorgeous, Caroline! It's awesome what items can mean so much to us, right? Got any other objects that you treasure, like that necklace? [image: a photo of a stack of bowls with different designs on them]
Caroline (D4:5): Yep, Melanie! I've got some other stuff with sentimental value, like my hand-painted bowl. A friend made it for my 18th birthday ten years ago. The pattern and colors are awesome-- it reminds me of art and self-expression.
Melanie (D4:6): That sounds great, Caroline! It's awesome having stuff around that make us think of good connections and times. Actually, I just took my fam camping in the mountains last week - it was a really nice time together!
Caroline (D4:7): Sounds great, Mel. Glad you made some new family mems. How was it? Anything fun?
Melanie (D4:8): It was an awesome time, Caroline! We explored nature, roasted marshmallows around the campfire and even went on a hike. The view from the top was amazing! The 2 younger kids love nature. It was so special having these moments together as a family - I'll never forget it!
Caroline (D4:9): That's awesome, Melanie! Family moments like that are so special. Glad y'all had such a great time.
Melanie (D4:10): Thanks, Caroline! Family time matters to me. What's up with you lately?
Caroline (D4:11): Lately, I've been looking into counseling and mental health as a career. I want to help people who have gone through the same things as me. [image: a photo of a book shelf with many books on it]
Melanie (D4:12): Sounds great! What kind of counseling and mental health services do you want to persue?
Caroline (D4:13): I'm still figuring out the details, but I'm thinking of working with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health. Last Friday, I went to an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop and it was really enlightening. They talked about different therapeutic methods and how to best work with trans people. Seeing how passionate these pros were about making a safe space for people like me was amazing.
Melanie (D4:14): Woah, Caroline, it sounds like you're doing some impressive work. It's inspiring to see your dedication to helping others. What motivated you to pursue counseling?
Caroline (D4:15): Thanks, Melanie. It really mattered. My own journey and the support I got made a huge difference. Now I want to help people go through it too. I saw how counseling and support groups improved my life, so I started caring more about mental health and understanding myself. Now I'm passionate about creating a safe, inviting place for people to grow.
Melanie (D4:16): Wow, Caroline! You've gained so much from your own experience. Your passion and hard work to help others is awesome. Keep it up, you're making a big impact!
Caroline (D4:17): Thanks, Melanie! Your kind words mean a lot.
Melanie (D4:18): Congrats Caroline! Good on you for going after what you really care about. [image: a photo of a book shelf filled with books in a room]

Melanie (D17:22): That's awesome, Caroline! You drew it? What does it mean to you?
